business_scope.primary_industry_name: Discretionary Portfolio Advisory for Multiple Private Client Families

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57 (BCBCA), ss. 10–13 (incorporation application and certificate), s. 19 (articles), s. 42 (registered office), s. 51 (share capital), ss. 102–124 (directors and officers), s. 199 (written resolutions); applicable companion regulations: B.C. Reg. 353/2004 (Company Act Clarification) and corporate registry forms under the BCBCA
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Consumer Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of British Columbia (Registrar of Companies)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) together with Notice of Articles (Form 9) and Articles of Incorporation, filed under s. 10 BCBCA via BC Corporate Online (OneStop business registry portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a BC ULC and no escrow or capital deposit requirement; shares may be issued for nominal consideration. However, for registration as a portfolio manager, BC Securities Commission and National Instrument 31-103 impose adjusted working capital requirements (minimum working capital or surety bond stipulations) as a condition of the operating licence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CA-ULC-ENTITY], adopted by unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting under s. 199(1) of the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia). WHEREAS the Company was incorporated by Certificate of Incorporation dated [date]. 1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The Board accepts the founding shareholder's subscription for 100 common shares at CAD $1.00 per share, payable in full upon issuance. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office shall be at [address], British Columbia; the officers are authorized to file the Notice of Articles with the Registrar. 3. OFFICERS: [Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] is appointed Chief Compliance Officer and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until removed. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be entered in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance and NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Consumer Services (Name Request Service, OneStop portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) criminal record-free name search report for the proposed corporate name (e.g. '[Name] Family Office ULC'). Verify the proposed name does not conflict with existing BC or federal trademarks/corporate names. Instructions: complete the online name request, pay the name reservation fee, and await examiner approval; name protection lasts 56 days for incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Exhibits explaining corporate name (if requested by the examiner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised name request within the 56-day reservation window; alternatively, incorporate with a numbered name (BC number + 'B.C. Unlimited Liability Company') and apply later for a name change under s. 27 BCBCA via Form 11.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constating Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporation solicitor (authorized legal professional) and proposed directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation (in BC Form 2 style), Notice of Articles (Form 9), consent to act as director (s. 124 BCBCA), and registered office consent (s. 42 BCBCA). For an Unlimited Liability Corporation, the articles must expressly state that shareholder liability is unlimited in accordance with s. 51 BCBCA. All directors and the incorporator must execute the documents; electronic signatures are acceptable under the Electronic Transactions Act, SBC 2001, c 10.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (Form 6 or equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Internal review and correction by the incorporation solicitor; if technical defects are later identified, amend the articles by Form 10 or file a court application under s. 11 BCBCA for certification correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with the Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Consumer Services (BC Corporate Online / OneStop)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Incorporation Application (Form 1) including the Notice of Articles (Form 9) and Articles of Incorporation through BC Corporate Online. Pay the applicable filing fee (CAD 299.85 online) using the registry's secure payment gateway. The system will issue a transaction number; the Registrar reviews the submission against the BCBCA, including constitutional and name compliance. Priority and standard processing options are available; standard online filings are typically completed within the stated SLA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, respond through BC Corporate Online within the deadline, supply correct information or amended documents, and refile; if rejected, restart with a corrected application and, where appropriate, seek the Registrar's discretion under s. 11 BCBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registry Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Consumer Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company's incorporation number and date. Verify the registry record (via BC Corporate Online company search) for accuracy of the registered office, director names, share structure, and unlimited liability designation. Download and securely store the certified PDF certificate.
required_dossiers: Registered office and director verification screenshot
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a correction of the certificate within 30 days under s. 11 BCBCA if clerical errors are found; re-register a new incorporation only if fundamental corrections are unavailable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations with CRA and BC Tax Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online), BC Ministry of Finance — Taxation Branch (OneStop), WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online using the Certificate of Incorporation; register for GST/HST if taxable revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 (annual), and for BC PST (8% on enumerated services) through the BC OneStop portal; register with WorkSafeBC as an employer for occupational injury compensation. Update the registered records office information with CRA within 15 days of any change.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, file a late registration with explanation under CRA's voluntary disclosure/administrative relief process; PST registrations may be backdated; WorkSafeBC penalties may be appealed through the Workers' Compensation Appeal Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Kit and Statutory Records Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office and Registered Records Office (professional corporate service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and maintain the corporate minute book: register the first board resolution, issue share certificates reflecting the approved subscription, create the register of directors, register of allotments, register of beneficial owners (for BC Transparency Act compliance), and the central securities register. Maintain the registered records office as required under s. 42 BCBCA. File any subsequent Form 10/11 changes with the Registrar (e.g. director changes, office changes).
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership register (BC Transparency Act, SBC 2019, c 23)
Registered office consent and records office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify omitted records by convening a directors' resolution and back-dating minutes in compliance with BCBCA; apply to court under s. 243 BCBCA for record access/correction if disputes arise; report any transparency register gaps to the Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC), Registration Division, in consultation with the Investment Industry Regulatory Organization of Canada (IIROC) or the Mutual Fund Dealers Association as applicable; municipal business licensing authority (City of Vancouver Licenses Branch or applicable municipality)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Portfolio Manager Registration (Registered Portfolio Manager) under s. 34 of the Securities Act, RSBC 1996, c 418, and National Instrument 31-103 Registration Requirements, Exemptions and Ongoing Registrant Obligations — Category: Discretionary Portfolio Advisory for Multiple Private Client Families (Multi-Family Office)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment Office, BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, in coordination with Environment and Climate Change Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Low-Impact Registration — Category D (commercial office premises): no reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2018, c 51; leasehold fit-out requires a municipal building permit and sanitary sewer connection approval; a full Environmental Impact Assessment report is not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with municipal sanitary sewer bylaws (e.g. City of Vancouver Sewer Use Bylaw 8093) — no industrial effluent discharge; indoor air quality and VOC limits per ASHRAE 62.1 and the BC Building Code; waste handling under the BC Recycling Regulation, B.C. Reg. 449/2004 (e-waste, printed paper and packaging) and the BC Hazardous Waste Regulation, B.C. Reg. 63/88 (exempt quantities for small-office hazardous waste); no stationary combustion emissions requiring a BC air discharge permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code (B.C. Reg. 142/2022) and municipal fire inspection; structural load inspection and building permit approval for office fit-out per the BC Building Code and local zoning bylaw; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance — employer registration (Form 7) and compliance with the Workers Compensation Act (injury prevention, ergonomic seating, emergency egress, and first aid requirements); physical security and business continuity measures for the multi-family office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) with online portal at canada.ca/cra
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities including non-resident corporations must apply for a Business Number (BN) as their statutory tax identification number. Non-residents register online via CRA My Business Account or by mail using Form RC59 if carrying on business in Canada or maintaining a permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections available under Canadian tax law. Classification is determined solely by residency status under the Income Tax Act and provincial rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: GST/HST returns filed electronically through CRA My Account. Digital record retention required for audits; no real-time fiscal clearance or automated digital stamping mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada and services performed outside Canada for non-resident clients qualify for 0% GST/PST rate. Must provide evidence of export and non-residency of the recipient.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False claims of zero-rating under the Excise Tax Act may result in penalties up to 50% of tax evaded, interest, fines, and potential criminal prosecution. Retrospective adjustments and audits are standard.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority. Official foreign-exchange reserve administration is exercised by the Department of Finance Canada through the Exchange Fund Account. Cross-border financial-transaction reporting and AML/ATF oversight are enforced by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, 2000 (PCMLTFA), with prudential regulation of Schedule I banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Canada has no central foreign-exchange control or licensing authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility as an IMF Article VIII member. No exchange-control approvals, currency allocation quotas, or repatriation licenses apply to dividend distributions, management fees, or redemption proceeds remitted externally by a BC-incorporated ULC. Practical remittance hurdles are: (1) CRA Part XIII withholding tax on payments to non-residents; (2) Schedule I bank release procedures requiring SWIFT purpose codes and sanctions screening; (3) FATCA and CRS self-certification for each beneficial owner; and (4) securities custody constraints requiring client discretionary assets to remain at a Canadian-regulated eligible custodian under the BC Securities Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canadian law imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory repatriation timelines, and no required conversion ratio for foreign-currency receipts. The ULC may freely retain, convert, or reinvest export or service-fee proceeds. The only analogous obligations are FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Reports and Electronic Funds Transfer Reports for transactions equal to or above C$10,000; these are information-reporting duties only and do not restrict currency convertibility or the ULC's use of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with US-dollar cross-border corridor

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW. A non-Canadian digital EMI cannot lawfully maintain a full corporate deposit account for a BC ULC because deposit-taking is restricted to banks chartered under the Bank Act (Canada). A foreign fintech may at most register with FINTRAC as a money services business and, where retail payment functions are performed, must transition to the Bank of Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) supervisory regime. For discretionary portfolio advisory under ISIC 6430, securities regulators additionally require custody of client assets at an eligible Canadian custodian; holding family-office client funds at an offshore EMI is non-compliant and could trigger unregistered MSB and unregistered dealer exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PCMLTFA imposes no absolute statutory obligation that directors appear physically for account opening; risk-based verification standards allow remote onboarding using dual-source identity documents and digital verification. In practice, however, Schedule I banks will require at least one director or officer with Canadian nexus to attend an in-person or video interview for a high-risk ULC carrying discretionary client-asset mandates. A notarized board resolution, current Register of Individuals with Significant Control, and a certified copy of the ULC Notice of Articles are generally demanded before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of wealth or substantial non-Canadian capital injection into the ULC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transactional source-of-wealth file: (i) audited financial statements of the originating family entity; (ii) notarized trust deeds or constitutional documents of the family office; (iii) bank reference from the remitting institution identifying the originator; (iv) up-to-date Register of Individuals with Significant Control for the BC ULC; and (v) sworn declarations from each founder disclaiming proceeds of crime and undisclosed tax liabilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hits on ultimate beneficial owners or family members
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions defense package: (i) global sanctions-screening report generated against OFAC, UN, EU, and Canadian Consolidated Automated Export/Screening lists; (ii) independent legal opinion confirming the absence of designated-party status; (iii) wire reference and SWIFT purpose codes for each antecedent transfer; (iv) completed politically exposed person questionnaire with a documented explanation of the political affiliation; and (v) any applicable exemption or regulator correspondence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires from high-risk, sanctioned, or FATF grey-listed remittance corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corridor compliance pack: (i) FATF jurisdiction risk memorandum rationale for the corridor; (ii) chain-of-custody wire flow diagram from originator to ULC account; (iii) full originator name, address, and international bank account identifiers; (iv) discretionary investment management agreement evidencing the underlying family-client relationship; and (v) negative news and adverse-media screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discretionary authority over third-party family assets triggering unregistered investment-fund or power-of-attorney concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Securities-registration defense: (i) BC Securities Commission exemption memorandum or registration confirmation; (ii) CIRO/IIROC membership or investment counsel registration proof; (iii) signed discretionary investment management agreements for each family; (iv) eligible Canadian custodian confirmation for client assets; and (v) legal opinion that the ULC does not constitute an investment fund or managed account scheme under applicable securities law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through classification of the ULC creating uncertainty as to the bank's withholding and beneficial-ownership obligations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax-transparency bundle: (i) CRA rulings or professional tax opinion on ULC classification; (ii) Part XIII withholding analysis prepared by Canadian tax counsel; (iii) FATCA Form W-8BEN-E or CRS self-certification for each non-resident member; (iv) ULC annual return and financial statements evidencing paid-in capital and equity structure; and (v) an explanation of the ULC's unlimited liability feature and its relevance to cross-border loan guarantees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital may be routed only via SWIFT wire from a recognized financial institution to the ULC's designated operational or escrow account. Wire instructions must contain the full ULC legal name and an explicit purpose, such as 'ULC Equity Subscription' or 'Capital Contribution', using a purpose-code taxonomy pre-approved by the receiving Schedule I bank's relationship management (commonly 'TRF', 'GIFT', or an institution-specific equity code) to avoid enhanced review. Verification is mandatory under PCMLTFA and includes UBO screening, Register of Individuals with Significant Control attestation, a certified copy of the ULC Notice of Articles, and a source-of-funds certificate. CAD wires settle same-day with final settlement via Lynx; USD wires use the bank's US-dollar correspondent corridor. Each inbound transfer equal to or above C$10,000 that is not a client-originated transaction requires a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements and portfolio transactions use: (i) SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfer with SWIFT GPI tracking for cross-border institutional payments; (ii) MT202 COV cover payments for correspondent-backed high-value transfers; (iii) commercial letters of credit for documentary trade lines; and (iv) Lynx same-day finality for large CAD domestic settlements. Each outbound wire equal to or above C$10,000 triggers a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report, and disbursement instructions must carry compliant purpose language (for example, 'Portfolio Subscription', 'Client Redemption Distribution', or 'Investment Disbursement') rather than ambiguous wealth-planning terminology.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD foreign exchange forward contracts with tenors up to 24 months under an IFEMA master agreement with a Schedule I bank counterparty
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD fixed-for-floating) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex for long-dated liability hedging
CME-listed CAD/USD futures contracts for short-term liquidity and cash-flow windows
OTC CAD/USD foreign exchange options with a Canadian-regulated or G7 dealer where the hedge is economically linked to a specific ULC liability or cash-flow exposure
Two-leg FX swaps used to manage seasonally mismatched subscription and distribution cash flows; NDF transactions are not permissible for CAD because a deep onshore deliverable market exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under Section 271 of the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies — BC Corporate Registry (Corporate Online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the company's anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation each calendar year; example: a March 31 incorporation date gives a May 31 filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No incremental late fee for an isolated delay, but unfiled annual reports create registry default status; two consecutive years of non-filing constitute a statutory ground for administrative strike-off and dissolution under s. 277 of the BC Business Corporations Act. Restoration requires payment of arrears, registrar or court approval, and applicable restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Form 31-103F1 Annual Information Form (registered investment counsel / portfolio manager / MFO licensure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC) through the National Registration Database (NRD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the MFO's financial year-end; a December 31 fiscal year-end requires filing by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continuous non-compliance exposes the securities registration to suspension, terms, conditions, or cancellation under the Securities Act (BC); late or incomplete filings typically trigger compliance review and possible enforcement proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Form 31-103F2 Annual Audited Financial Statements (securities registrant)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 120 days after the MFO's financial year-end; a December 31 fiscal year-end requires filing by April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver audited annual financial statements within the prescribed period is a registrant default that may result in suspension, cancellation, or imposition of terms and conditions, and may be referred to BCSC enforcement or a regulatory proceeding.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: BC private-company legislation does not impose a universal revenue or asset threshold for audit; audit becomes mandatory for this MFO because the BC ULC is a securities-registered investment counsel/portfolio manager that must deliver audited Form 31-103F2 financial statements to the BCSC. An audit may also be required by the articles, unanimous shareholder agreement, director resolution, court or registrar order, or another regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Canadian generally accepted accounting principles under the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for public reporting constituents and ASPE for the private operating ULC / MFO, subject to securities regulator requirements; audits are performed under Canadian Auditing Standards (CAS).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BC annual report certification requires the company to attest that its corporate records are current. A share transfer must be approved by the directors, recorded in the Register of Transfers, and reflected in the Register of Members before the next annual confirmation is signed. UBO / individuals-with-significant-control records must be updated within the prescribed change period after a transfer, generally no later than 15 days after the company becomes aware, and reconciled with the annual report confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control / UBO Register (where prescribed)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – 900 per year for BC registered office, records office, registered agent, and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 – 18,000 per year for a securities-registered ULC / multi-family office discretionary advisory entity
